title: Vona Well Depth and Drilling Cost
meta_description: Vona wells have a 140-foot median depth; see local yields, water levels, drilling costs, and risks before buying land.
h1: Vona, Colorado Well Depth, Yield, and Drilling Costs
intro_html:
Buying land near Vona means understanding what the local well records can—and cannot—tell you. Within 5 miles of Vona, Colorado DWR records show 178 permitted wells. Of those, 80 are recorded as constructed, 107 report a total depth, 24 report a pump yield, and 7 report a static water level.

The local record points to generally moderate well depths and useful reported yields, but the information is uneven from one parcel to the next. A nearby well is useful evidence, not a guarantee. Before closing or building, match neighboring permits with a site-specific driller's review, water-right requirements, septic planning, and the intended household or livestock use.

sections.heading: Vona well depths: mostly shallow plains wells
sections.html:
The median reported well depth near Vona is 140 feet. The middle half runs from 111 to 159 feet, and 90% of reported wells are 180 feet or shallower. The deepest well in the record is 228 feet. Depth is concentrated in the 100-to-300-foot range, which accounts for 85% of the depth mix; 15% are under 100 feet.

For a drilling bid, that middle range is more useful than the median alone. A contractor will still price the actual geology, access, casing, grout, and completion materials at your lot. The records name 121 wells in unnamed or fractured-bedrock aquifers, 54 in the Ogallala, and 1 in the High Plains Aquifer. That mix makes neighboring construction details worth checking, especially where fractured rock can produce variable results.

sections.heading: Reported well yields around Vona
sections.html:
Only 24 wells report a pump yield, so the yield statistics are a guide rather than a guarantee for every parcel. Among those reports, the median yield is 15.5 gallons per minute, with the middle half from 9.8 to 26.2 gallons per minute. The reported mix is favorable on paper: 62% produce more than 15 gallons per minute, 29% fall from 5 to 15, and 8% from 1 to 5.

No reported well is under 1 gallon per minute in this dataset. That does not eliminate low-yield or dry-hole risk on an untested lot. Ask for the well completion report, pump test information, and any production limitations. A household-use well also has Colorado rules, including the 35-gallon-per-minute exempt-well pumping limit, and other uses may require different water-right or augmentation-plan review.

sections.heading: What the water levels show near Vona
sections.html:
The 7 wells reporting static water levels have a median depth to water of 118 feet. The middle half is 102 to 120 feet below ground. These readings help a driller estimate pump setting and equipment needs, but they are not a complete groundwater trend for Vona.

There are too few reported static levels to conclude that the water table is dropping or stable. Permit activity spans the 1950s through the 2020s, with the newest permit year 2024, but permit dates are not water-level measurements. Treat the local water level as parcel-specific. Before buying, obtain current information from nearby wells and have a contractor evaluate pump placement, pressure-tank requirements, and the distance between the water level and the planned building.

sections.heading: Vona permit history and local drillers
sections.html:
The permit record shows activity in several periods rather than a steady yearly pattern. Records include 2 permits from the 1950s, 8 from the 1960s, 32 from the 1970s, 9 from the 1980s, 22 from the 1990s, 20 from the 2000s, 9 from the 2010s, and 7 from the 2020s. The newest permit year is 2024.

Schaal Drilling Co., listed as Schaal, Ruben T., appears most often with 28 wells. Parrish Drilling, listed as Parrish, Wayne, appears on 9, and Klassen Drilling, listed as Klassen, Paul C., appears on 8. Those records can help identify local experience around Vona, Seibert, and Stratton. Confirm current licensing, availability, scope of work, and references before selecting a driller.

sections.heading: What a new Vona well may cost
sections.html:
For Vona's alluvium and plains sedimentary rock, the drilling model uses a typical rate of $35 to $55 per foot. At the 140-foot median depth, the drilled hole is estimated at about $4,900 to $7,700. That is only the drilling portion, not a complete water system.

A finished well with pump, tank, trenching, and electrical is modeled at about $10,900 to $19,700 at the median depth. Your bid can change with access, casing and grout requirements, rock conditions, pump size, electrical distance, and the need for additional testing or treatment. Get the drilling and completion assumptions in writing. A low initial price may not include the equipment and site work needed to deliver water to the house.

sections.heading: Risks to check before buying or building near Vona
sections.html:
Yield and depth are not the only concerns. Within about 10 miles of Vona, the mapped environmental record includes 3 PFAS sampling or contamination sites and 1 EPA Superfund or cleanup site. It also shows 0 historic mine features. These mapped sites do not establish contamination at your parcel, but they justify checking the location, groundwater direction, and available testing history before relying on a well.

Review the well permit, construction report, water quality results, and septic location together. Keep the well and septic system separated as required by applicable rules, and confirm that the lot has room for the house, replacement septic area, access, and drilling equipment. Colorado DWR permit conditions and water-right requirements can limit use, particularly for irrigation, stock, or additional buildings.

sections.heading: A practical Vona lot-buying plan
sections.html:
Start by collecting permits and completion reports for wells closest to the property, not just the overall Vona statistics. Compare their depths, reported yields, aquifers, static water levels, and intended uses. Nearby Seibert and Stratton may provide useful regional context, but conditions can change across the plains, so they should not replace parcel-specific investigation.

Before closing, make the well a documented part of due diligence. Have a Colorado driller review access and likely construction, verify the water-right pathway for the planned use, and budget the full system rather than drilling alone. If you are building, coordinate the well, septic system, driveway, electrical route, and house location before excavation begins. For an existing well, test both the water quality and the operating equipment instead of assuming a permitted well is a producing, potable well.

faq.q: How deep are wells in Vona, Colorado?
faq.a: The median reported well depth within 5 miles of Vona is 140 feet. The middle half runs from 111 to 159 feet, and the deepest recorded well is 228 feet. Most wells are in the 100-to-300-foot range. The actual depth at a new lot depends on local geology, the aquifer encountered, and the driller's construction requirements.

faq.q: What does it cost to drill a well in Vona?
faq.a: The local cost model uses $35 to $55 per foot for alluvium and plains sedimentary rock. At the 140-foot median depth, drilling alone is about $4,900 to $7,700. A finished system with pump, tank, trenching, and electrical is modeled at $10,900 to $19,700. Site access, casing, grout, equipment, and electrical distance can change the bid.

faq.q: How much water do Vona wells produce?
faq.a: Among the 24 wells that report a pump yield, the median is 15.5 gallons per minute, with the middle half from 9.8 to 26.2. Reported yields include 62% above 15 gallons per minute and 8% from 1 to 5. Because yield data is limited, these figures do not guarantee production on an untested parcel.

faq.q: Is well water safe to drink in Vona?
faq.a: A permit or reported yield does not prove that water is safe to drink. The area has 3 mapped PFAS sampling or contamination sites within about 10 miles and 1 EPA Superfund or cleanup site. Test the specific well for relevant contaminants, review nearby environmental sites, and use treatment only after testing identifies what is present.

faq.q: Is the water table dropping near Vona?
faq.a: The available records do not establish a groundwater trend. Only 7 wells report static water levels; their median depth to water is 118 feet, with the middle half from 102 to 120 feet. Permit activity extends through 2024, but permit dates are not water-level measurements. Ask for current readings from nearby wells and have a driller assess the parcel.
